correctness.rationale: The three nowhere-simultaneously-vanishing Frobenius sections give a rank-two kernel bundle and a genuine smooth P1-bundle. Its Chern polynomial 1-qh+q^2h^2 yields the integral ring by the projective-bundle formula, with CH^3 generated by h^2u of degree 1 and triple intersection cubic 3ab(a+qb). The binary-cubic discriminant 81q^2 is unchanged by every unimodular reparametrization of CH^1 or sign change of its degree map, proving classification for every positive height. Explicit reductions produce the residue-field and rational equivalences, and P1 fibers give the zeta function. The executable exact arithmetic only checks sample cases and does not replace any universal step.

originality.rationale: The 2026 same-object study supplies Picard rank and geometric nonisomorphism, but not the unmarked integral Chow-ring invariant or the all-prime-field multiplicative blindness. The 2017 same-example motivic comparison establishes additive Chow-group equivalence (Lemma 5.2) rather than ring equivalence, leaving exactly the multiplicative distinction at issue. Shimada 2011 treats a codimension-two two-equation incidence instead. The proof does apply standard projective-bundle and binary-cubic inputs, so priority of the short computation has a specific unresolved earlier-literature risk, notably the inaccessible 1993 unseparated-flags chapter.

value.rationale: The family is a natural minimal-dimensional rank-two-Picard model of non-smooth parabolic homogeneous geometry from new literature. Classifying its entire family of abstract integral Chow rings is a natural exact invariant problem. The integral cubic detects an exponent entirely invisible in every prime-field Chow-ring reduction, the rational ring, and the common finite-field zeta function, demonstrating a concrete arithmetic obstruction to reconstructing integral multiplication from these simpler data. It is not presented as a novel general projective-bundle formula, and the independent-historical-priority limitations are explicit.
